threat_model.recipient: Elisa product team. No raw-data access, no hashing keys, no enb->area mapping, no auxiliary identity data (relative approach, EDPS v SRB).
threat_model.worst_case: Knows some true (enb, time) points about a target, public enb->province geography, and - for the differencing test - the true per-slice totals.

attacks.name: Row uniqueness
attacks.attacker_knowledge: QI values of a target (same under both models)
attacks.baseline_raw: 36.31% of subscribers own at least one unique row (QI set D)
attacks.interpretation: k-anonymity on distinct subscribers removes singling out by QI: the expected chance of picking the target's row is 1 in 40.

attacks.name: Trajectory attack
attacks.attacker_knowledge: p known (location, time) points for a target, p = 1..4
attacks.baseline_raw: 4 known (enb, hour) points uniquely identify 99.6% of eligible subscribers

record.structural_defence: The record release carries no subscriber key, so an attacker cannot group a target's rows together. The figures below assume the strictly stronger attacker who somehow can - they bound the risk.

attacks.interpretation: Rows are not linkable, so the raw 99.6% collapses. Even granting an attacker the ability to link, 4 known points leave a median of 1.0 candidate subscribers and single out 99.3% of targets.

attacks.name: Homogeneity (l-diversity)
attacks.attacker_knowledge: QI values of a target (same under both models)
attacks.baseline_raw: Not applicable: raw rows are individually identifying

record.note: application_category is excluded: it is a quasi-identifier, so every group holds one value by construction.

attacks.interpretation: No group is homogeneous on the revealing (True) value for any of the three attributes, so k-anonymity is not leaking a positive trait here. Homogeneous groups are common but they are homogeneous on False (e.g. 94.1702% for 'video'), which discloses only that a target did not do something.

attacks.name: Outliers
attacks.attacker_knowledge: QI values plus the target's approximate data volume
attacks.baseline_raw: 1.00% of subscribers above the volume p99; 0.019% unique at 0.1 GB rounding
attacks.interpretation: Top-coding collapses the extreme tail, but adding a 0.1 GB volume bucket to the QI still puts 2.01176% of rows below k, and leaves 16850 heavy-user rows there. Volume is not part of the k-anonymity QI set, so this is residual risk.

attacks.name: Differencing on aggregates
attacks.attacker_knowledge: worst_case: the true n_subscribers total per (time_bucket, province) slice
attacks.baseline_raw: Not applicable: raw has no suppression to undo

aggregate.realistic: Not attemptable: the recipient does not hold true slice totals.

attacks.interpretation: No slice in this extract ever loses exactly one cell, so the subtraction never isolates a single suppressed value: recovery is 0.0% even undefended (no noise, no secondary suppression). The attack is blocked by the shape of the data here, NOT demonstrably by secondary suppression - which costs 80 extra cells and remains untested on this extract. The synthetic test in tests/test_evaluate.py shows the defence works when a lone cell is suppressed.

attacks.name: Membership inference on aggregates
attacks.attacker_knowledge: worst_case: every other subscriber's data and the target's true cells - the standard differential-privacy adversary
attacks.baseline_raw: 100% - raw rows carry the subscriber key outright

aggregate.method: For each target the attacker sees one noisy release drawn at random from the world with or without them, and applies a Laplace likelihood-ratio test over the target's cells. 50% = random guessing.
aggregate.scope_note: The test operates on the noised counts, which is exactly what the DP guarantee covers. Suppression is not simulated per target, so this measures the count channel only.
aggregate.realistic: Not attemptable: the recipient does not hold the other subscribers' data.

attacks.interpretation: Without noise the attacker is 100.0% accurate. At the deployed epsilon the attack falls to 54.005% against a theoretical ceiling of 73.1059%, i.e. an advantage of 8.01 points over guessing.
